ActiveEtfHoldingWeightRow.description:
One constituent's FULL current-day weight — every holding on `report_date`, not just the
ones that changed (`ActiveEtfReportRow`'s own scope). This is the 成分股/產業分佈 tab's real
backing: a 成分股 donut/table needs the whole holdings list with weight, and a 產業分佈 view
needs each holding's industry — neither is expressible from the diffed change rows alone.
`industry_category` is joined from the same whole-market `STOCK_INFO_JOB` roster
`GetSectorHeatmapTool` already reads (ingest-owned store, never a live per-symbol fetch);
`None` when the constituent isn't found in that day's roster (never fabricated).
ActiveEtfHoldingWeightRow.title: ActiveEtfHoldingWeightRow

ActiveEtfReportRow.description:
One constituent's row in the 操作日報 — only constituents with a nonzero buy/sell that
day appear (FinMind's `HoldingChange` is already filtered to changed rows).
ActiveEtfReportRow.title: ActiveEtfReportRow

AdvanceDeclineBuckets.description:
Symbol counts bucketed by close-to-close percentage change. `unchanged` is exactly
`pct_change == 0`; every other symbol falls into exactly one up- or down-side bucket.
AdvanceDeclineBuckets.title: AdvanceDeclineBuckets

AlertPreference.description:
One row per user — the default channels + digest + quiet-hours applied when a rule/job
doesn't override them.
AlertPreference.title: AlertPreference

AnalystConsensus.description:
`analyst_consensus` — the licensed analyst-ratings/target-price gap (yfinance).

The `_extended` fields are populated only for non-TW markets, where yfinance's analyst
coverage is primary rather than a sparse gap-filler — TW payloads never set them, so the
existing narrow TW shape is unaffected.
AnalystConsensus.title: AnalystConsensus

AttachmentBlock.description:
Metadata + (for documents) extracted text for one user-uploaded chat attachment.

Deliberately **never** carries the raw file/image bytes — those are ephemeral, living only
in-memory for the one turn's LLM call (see `api/routers/agent.py`'s `AttachmentInput` and
`attachments/extractor.py`), never persisted here past that turn, mirroring this codebase's
"don't persist a raw blob where a smaller derived form suffices" discipline
(`governance.md`'s no-raw-payload-logging principle, applied to user-uploaded content
rather than model/source output). `extracted_text` is the `markitdown`-converted Markdown
for a document attachment (`.docx`/`.xlsx`/`.pptx`/`.pdf`/...); it is `None` for an image
attachment (images go to the LLM as vision input for that turn only, never through
`markitdown`, and are not re-derivable as text here).
AttachmentBlock.title: AttachmentBlock

AttachmentInput.description:
One chat attachment as sent by the client — the whole file inline as base64, mirroring
`voice.py`'s `audio_base64` idiom (base64-in-JSON, not multipart).
AttachmentInput.title: AttachmentInput

AttentionListEntry.description: The symbol appears on the exchange 注意股 list.
AttentionListEntry.title: AttentionListEntry

BatchAlertItem.description: One stock's own rule in a per-stock batch.
BatchAlertItem.title: BatchAlertItem

BatchCreateAlertsRequest.description:
Several per-stock rules created together (「逐檔設定」): each item has its own stock and
its own level; frequency, lifetime and channels are shared.
BatchCreateAlertsRequest.title: BatchCreateAlertsRequest

BranchSummaryBlock.description:
A structured decision+cause summary of an abandoned branch — never free prose, per the
"carry the conclusion, drop the transcript" rule shared with `CompactionEntry`.
BranchSummaryBlock.title: BranchSummaryBlock

BuildConversationPackageOutput.description: M5N Conversation Package — the AI-safe caveated artifact for one symbol.
BuildConversationPackageOutput.title: BuildConversationPackageOutput

BusinessIndicatorRow.description:
`business_indicator` — one month's 景氣對策信號 (business/economic-climate indicator)
reading. Backer/Sponsor-only; market-level, no symbol scope; released on the statutory
monthly cadence, not a daily-clock-time snapshot.
BusinessIndicatorRow.title: BusinessIndicatorRow

CalendarEventOut.description:
Tool-output mirror of `calendar.models.CalendarEvent` — a distinct type from that
module's own model so `tools/` never re-exports a `calendar/`-owned Pydantic model
directly as a tool's `output_model` (keeps the tool-output schema decoupled from that
module's internal shape).
CalendarEventOut.title: CalendarEventOut

CandlestickPatternHit.description:
One completed candlestick-pattern match (`analytics/patterns.py`) at a given bar.
`direction` is a plain descriptive label — `+1` (看多/bullish-leaning), `-1`
(看空/bearish-leaning), or `0` (doji — no directional read) — never a buy/sell instruction
(governance §7 non-trading).
CandlestickPatternHit.title: CandlestickPatternHit

Capability.description: What callers request — never a source id.
Capability.title: Capability

CapabilitySummary.description: One capability's redacted provenance summary — never the raw `payload` dict.
CapabilitySummary.title: CapabilitySummary

CentralBankRateRow.description:
`central_bank_rate` — one central bank's policy-rate reading (`symbol` is the bank code,
e.g. FED/BOE/ECB/BOJ). Free tier; event-driven (announced at policy-meeting dates, not a
daily-clock-time series). Modeled `Market.GLOBAL` — this is inherently a multi-country panel
with no single-country home; forcing any one country's `Market` value onto a dozen distinct
central banks would misrepresent the data's actual scope.
CentralBankRateRow.title: CentralBankRateRow

ChannelStatus.description: Which external channels can actually reach this user right now.
ChannelStatus.title: ChannelStatus

ChartHint.description:
A declarative visualization hint: `mark` + channel encodings, resolved by the frontend
renderer against the tool's own row data. Optional on every output model that carries one —
absence means "no generic-chart opinion," not an error; the existing hardcoded `card_type`
path still renders that tool's card exactly as it does today.
ChartHint.title: ChartHint

ChipBrokerNetSummary.description:
One broker/branch's total net buy/sell (`sum(buy - sell)`) over the whole fetched range —
see `_top_broker_net_summary`'s docstring for why this exists: the same architecture gap as
`InstitutionalFlowRollingNet` (Finding #69), one tool over. `get_chip_flows` can return
thousands of per-day per-branch rows (a live repro against 鴻海/2317 returned 6,500+), and
without a pre-aggregated summary the model was observed spending its entire response budget
manually eyeballing/summing individual 分點 rows, leaving zero room for prose — this field
is what it should cite instead.
ChipBrokerNetSummary.title: ChipBrokerNetSummary

ChipBrokerRow.description: `chip_broker` — one branch(分點)/broker trading row for one trading day. Sponsor-only.
ChipBrokerRow.title: ChipBrokerRow

ChipBrokerTopRow.description:
One broker's row in the 買超Top15/賣超Top15 table (`chip-analysis-panel.tsx`'s own
`BrokerTopRow`, now computed here instead of client-side so an unentitled caller's
row-preview mask (governance.md §4 top-N-preview exception) can apply to the SAME ranked
rows the frontend renders, not to the raw per-day feed underneath them). `rank` (1-based,
within this row's own buy-top or sell-top list) is the only field that survives masking.
ChipBrokerTopRow.title: ChipBrokerTopRow

ClosePrice.description: Closing price is above/below a level the user chose.
ClosePrice.title: ClosePrice

ConversationFactOut.description:
One Mode-C fact, passed through from `context/conversation.py` unchanged (already
payload-free).
ConversationFactOut.title: ConversationFactOut

CrudeOilPricesRow.description:
`crude_oil_prices` — one day's WTI/Brent crude spot-price reading. Free tier; `symbol` is
the benchmark name (WTI/Brent). Modeled `Market.GLOBAL` — a world commodity benchmark, no
single-country home. This is a **spot price, not a real-time quote** — the latest available
date is typically several trading days (~1 week) behind, unlike futures real-time quotes;
always read the actually-returned latest `date`, don't assume same-day freshness.
CrudeOilPricesRow.title: CrudeOilPricesRow

DailyChange.description: Single-day move versus the prior trading day's close reaches a percentage.
DailyChange.title: DailyChange

DailySignalHighlight.description:
One 焦點股 highlight card — the single stock with the largest aggregate inflow/outflow
for the day, plus the 多空共識 (buying-vs-selling ETF count) for that same stock. Unlike
`DailySignalRow`, this is never part of the "top N free rows" budget — governance.md §4's
row-preview exception locks it entirely (`locked=True`, every field but that flag nulled)
for an unentitled caller, since a single 焦點股 highlight concentrates the whole card's most
valuable signal into one card and giving it away for free would defeat the point of gating
the rest of the list.
DailySignalHighlight.title: DailySignalHighlight

DailySignalRow.description:
One constituent stock's day-over-day status across EVERY active ETF combined — the same
新增/刪除/加碼/減碼 classification `ActiveEtfReportRow` uses for one ETF, applied to the
aggregate (sum of shares held across all active ETFs) instead. Only stocks with a nonzero
aggregate change appear (mirrors `ActiveEtfReportRow`'s own "only changed rows" contract).
`locked=True` rows (governance.md §4 top-N-preview exception) have every field but `status`/
`rank` nulled server-side, including `component_stock_id`/`component_stock_name` — an
unentitled caller must not learn which stock a locked row even names.
DailySignalRow.title: DailySignalRow

DataClass.description: The single access gate — vendor-neutral licensed/paid vs free.
DataClass.title: DataClass

DayTradingRow.description: `day_trading` — one day-trading (當沖) eligibility/volume row for one stock.
DayTradingRow.title: DayTradingRow

DirectorShareholding.description:
`shareholding` — one 董監事持股餘額 (director/supervisor shareholding) row for one
reporting month.
DirectorShareholding.title: DirectorShareholding

DispositionBoardCardRow.description:
`disposition_board` — one 處置王-style card, `GetDispositionBoardTool`'s output row.
Joins `AttentionStockRow`/`DispositionEventRow` (bucket classification + projection) against
`PRICE_EOD_JOB` closes and `INSTITUTIONAL_FLOW_JOB` flow (both already-ingested, whole-
market) plus a bounded per-symbol `get_margin_short` fan-out (never a live whole-market
scan). `projection_caveat` is always populated — states plainly that
`days_until_next_disposition` is this codebase's own rule-based encoding of TWSE's publicly
stated escalation pattern, not a verbatim TWSE-published number, and is bounded by however
much attention-flag history has accumulated since this feature's ingest jobs first ran.
Three buckets (風險股/處置中/即將出關); 自結發布 is not a 4th bucket — it's a per-card
enrichment (`self_assessed_*` fields below), since a company's preliminary-earnings filing
is orthogonal to its attention/disposition status, not a bucket of its own.
DispositionBoardCardRow.title: DispositionBoardCardRow

DispositionListEntry.description: The symbol appears on the exchange 處置股 (disposition) list.
DispositionListEntry.title: DispositionListEntry

DispositionSecuritiesRow.description:
`disposition_securities` — one 公布處置有價證券 (disposition-securities announcement) row
for one stock. Backer/Sponsor-only.
DispositionSecuritiesRow.title: DispositionSecuritiesRow

DividendCalendarEventRow.description:
One ETF's dividend event landing within the requested month, on any of its three
dates (`ex_dividend_date`/`last_buy_date`/`payment_date`) — the same row appears under
each date it actually has, so the calendar view can group by day without re-deriving
which dates belong to which event.
DividendCalendarEventRow.title: DividendCalendarEventRow

DividendFillResult.description:
Whether one settled ex-dividend event's price recovered to `before_price` — 填息
(cash/combined ex-dividend) or 填權 (stock-only) — before the stock's *next* ex-dividend
event, or (for the most recent event) as of the latest available close. `filled` is `None`,
never `False`, when there is not yet enough later price history to answer either way (the
next event hasn't happened yet AND no later close has reached `before_price`) — an unresolved
event is not the same fact as a failed one.
DividendFillResult.title: DividendFillResult

DividendPolicyStats.description:
The stats-strip figures above the 股利政策 chart — 綜合股利/現金殖利率/配息率/填息成功率,
all pre-computed server-side from `events`/`fill_results`/`latest_eps`/`latest_close` so the
frontend never re-derives a payout ratio or fill-rate from raw rows itself (same "cite the
pre-computed figure directly" convention `MonthRevenueTrendPoint` documents). Any figure is
`None`, never a fabricated 0, when its own inputs are missing.
DividendPolicyStats.title: DividendPolicyStats

DividendResultRow.description: `dividend_result` — one 除權除息結果 (ex-dividend/ex-rights result) row for one stock.
DividendResultRow.title: DividendResultRow

DividendYearSummary.description:
One calendar year's dividend total — the 股利政策 chart's per-year bar (cash+stock
stacked) and the stats-strip's "latest year" figures, both derived from the same bucketing
so the chart and the headline numbers can never disagree.
DividendYearSummary.title: DividendYearSummary

EarningsCalendarRow.description:
`earnings_calendar` — one upcoming/recent earnings-report event row (`yfinance.Calendars`
market-wide feed, not scoped to one symbol's own `.calendar`).
EarningsCalendarRow.title: EarningsCalendarRow

EconomicCalendarRow.description:
`economic_calendar` — one macro-release event row (`yfinance.Calendars`); modeled
`Market.GLOBAL` since the underlying feed spans multiple countries/regions, distinguished
only by the free-text `region` field.
EconomicCalendarRow.title: EconomicCalendarRow

EntitlementView.description:
The resolved capability envelope for one user — what `GET /me` surfaces and what the
API/agent consult. Purely a projection of `entitlements` over the user's tier + BYOK
state; it holds no policy of its own.
EntitlementView.title: EntitlementView

EsgScore.description: `esg` — Sustainalytics-derived ESG risk score (large-cap only, sparse coverage).
EsgScore.title: EsgScore

EtfExpenseInfo.description:
`etf_expense_ratio` — internal-fee (內扣費用) disclosure for one fund/ETF, sourced from
SITCA's (投信投顧公會) monthly fee-rate report. `management_fee_pct`/`custody_fee_pct` are the
two disclosed line items; a true total-expense-ratio (內扣總費用率, TER) is approximated as
their sum via `total_expense_ratio_pct_approx` and DOES NOT include other operating costs, so
it is a floor, not the audited TER — the caveat says so. Any field is `None` when SITCA does
not disclose it for this fund (never fabricated).
EtfExpenseInfo.title: EtfExpenseInfo

EtfFundInfo.description:
`etf_holdings` (fund-level slice) — issuer/units-outstanding/tracked-index reference
data for a listed ETF. Does **not** carry per-constituent weights (issuer PCF holdings
remain an unfilled gap) — this is fund-level metadata only, refreshed on the issuer's
reporting cadence, not a live figure.
EtfFundInfo.title: EtfFundInfo

EtfHoldingRankRow.description:
One ETF's current holding of the target stock — the 持有張數排行 sub-view's row shape.
`locked=True` rows (governance.md §4 top-N-preview exception) have EVERY field nulled
server-side, including `etf_symbol`/`etf_name` — an unentitled caller must not learn which
ETF a locked row even belongs to, only that it exists (via `rank`, its 1-based position in
the full ranked list, which is not sensitive on its own).
EtfHoldingRankRow.title: EtfHoldingRankRow

EtfListRow.description:
One row of the whole-market ETF list — see `GetEtfListTool`'s own docstring for exactly
which already-ingested dataset backs each field. A field is `None` when its backing dataset
has no row for this symbol on this date — never fabricated to fill the column.
EtfListRow.title: EtfListRow

EtfMoneyFlowRow.description:
One constituent stock's cross-ETF aggregation row. `locked=True` rows (governance.md §4
top-N-preview exception) have every field but `rank` nulled server-side — an unentitled
caller must not learn which stock a locked row even names.
EtfMoneyFlowRow.title: EtfMoneyFlowRow

EtfNavRow.description:
`etf_nav` — one ETF's premium/discount-to-NAV snapshot, sourced from TWSE MIS's free,
keyless, whole-market `all_etf.txt` feed (issuer-published estimated NAV, relayed by TWSE —
not TWSE's own calculation; see the upstream page's own disclaimer). `premium_discount_pct`
is TWSE's own published 預估折溢價幅度 figure (`(close_price - estimated_nav) /
estimated_nav * 100`, confirmed live against several symbols), passed through as-is rather
than recomputed here, so this row never silently diverges from what investors see on the
source page. `prior_day_nav` is the fund's last confirmed (non-estimated) NAV — the
estimated NAV is provisional/intraday and can be revised by the issuer.

Note: units_outstanding is a leading indicator of unusual creation/redemption activity, not
itself a premium/discount signal — surfaced for completeness since the upstream feed already
carries it in the same row.
EtfNavRow.title: EtfNavRow

EtfPositionEvent.description:
One ETF's day-over-day change in its holding of the target stock — 建倉/清倉 (opening/
fully closing the position) or 加碼/減碼 (a same-day increase/decrease while still held) —
the 建清倉 sub-view's row shape. `event` is any `HoldingStatus` value except
`NO_PRIOR_DATA` (a day with no prior snapshot to diff against emits no event at all).
`locked` — see `EtfHoldingRankRow`; a locked event keeps its real `event_date`/`event`
classification (the timeline's own axis, not identifying) but nulls `etf_symbol`/`etf_name`/
`shares_delta` — an unentitled caller must not learn which ETF made the move.
EtfPositionEvent.title: EtfPositionEvent

EtfPositionEventCounts.description:
新增/刪除/加碼/減碼 counts across `position_events` — the summary-strip shape, mirroring
`GetDailySignalOutput`'s own `new_count`/`removed_count`/`increased_count`/`decreased_count`
fields (same four-way classification, scoped to one stock instead of the whole market).
EtfPositionEventCounts.title: EtfPositionEventCounts

EtfPremiumDiscount.description:
An ETF's 預估折溢價 (estimated premium/discount to NAV, TWSE's own published figure) is at
least `percent` on the chosen side. Applies to ETF codes only — a stock has no NAV row.
EtfPremiumDiscount.title: EtfPremiumDiscount

EtfScoreBreakdown.description:
The 4-factor breakdown for an ETF — deliberately NOT `StockScoreBreakdown`'s value/
quality/trend-template factors, which are either meaningless (an ETF has no ROE/EV-EBITDA of
its own) or actively misleading (the Minervini trend template misreads a stretched
leveraged/inverse ETF as bullish exactly when its daily-rebalancing decay risk peaks) for a
fund rather than an operating company.

- `momentum`: same 12-1 calculation as the stock breakdown — meaningful as fund performance.
- `premium_discount`: TWSE's own published 預估折溢價幅度 (estimated premium/discount to
  NAV) — the textbook ETF-quality metric with no stock equivalent.
- `cost`: SITCA-disclosed expense ratio percentile (lower cost ranks higher) — every ETF has
  one; no stock does.
- `management_activity`: holdings-turnover-derived, ACTIVE ETFs only — genuinely unavailable
  (not fabricated) for passive/leveraged/inverse ETFs, which have no holdings data ingested.
- `liquidity_flow`: 三大法人 institutional net-buy trend — the same chip sub-signal the stock
  breakdown's `revenue_flow` uses, without the (ETF-inapplicable) 月營收 half.
EtfScoreBreakdown.title: EtfScoreBreakdown

EtfTrailingReturns.description:
`etf_trailing_returns` — one listed ETF's price-return over 6 fixed trailing horizons
(1個月/1季/半年/1年/3年/5年), computed from ONE split/dividend-adjusted price history fetch
(`yfinance.Ticker.history(period="5y", auto_adjust=True)`) — never yfinance's own `.info`
fields (`ytdReturn`/`threeYearAverageReturn`/`fiveYearAverageReturn`), which mix inconsistent
units (percent vs. fraction, confirmed live) and don't cover 1M/1Q/6M/1Y at all. Computing
every horizon the same way over the same already-adjusted series means the six numbers are
genuinely comparable to each other, not stitched from two different methodologies.

`auto_adjust=True` retroactively folds every split/dividend into the historical close
series — this is deliberately NOT the raw `Capability.PRICE_EOD` bars this codebase ingests
elsewhere (those are unadjusted; see `get_fund_comparison`'s own dividend-reinvestment
simulation, built for exactly that gap, but which itself broke on 0050's real 2025-06-18
4-for-1 split precisely because the ingested bars are unadjusted — this capability sidesteps
that whole class of bug by reading Yahoo's pre-adjusted series instead).

A horizon is `None` (never fabricated) when the 5-year history window doesn't reach back
far enough for that horizon (e.g. a fund listed 2 years ago has no real 5-year return).
EtfTrailingReturns.title: EtfTrailingReturns

EtfWeightRankRow.description:
One ETF's current weighting of the target stock in ITS OWN portfolio — the 權重排行
sub-view's row shape. `locked` — see `EtfHoldingRankRow`.
EtfWeightRankRow.title: EtfWeightRankRow

ExchangeRateRow.description:
`exchange_rate` — one day's TWD-vs-foreign-currency reference rate row. Free tier;
`symbol` is the foreign-currency code (e.g. USD/EUR/JPY), TWD is implicit as the other leg.
Modeled `Market.TW`-scoped: this is a TWD-context dataset (the counter-currency is always
TWD), not a generic world-FX table.
ExchangeRateRow.title: ExchangeRateRow

FactorCatalog.description:
The full per-market catalog `get_factor_catalog` returns: boolean signal tags (TW only —
US/ETF have no batch-computed tag partition) plus numeric factor fields grouped by family.
FactorCatalog.title: FactorCatalog

FactorField.description:
One filterable factor. `key` is the token `run_screener`'s `conditions[].factor` expects.
`min`/`max`/`step` bound the slider; `None` for an enum-like field (`op_set` = `{eq, in}`
only), which instead lists its choices in `enum_values`. `source_field` is the underlying
upstream field name the engine maps this key to (a yfinance screener field for US/ETF, or a
`stock_scores` column name for TW) — kept alongside the bilingual label so the engine and the
catalog never drift apart.
FactorField.title: FactorField

FactorOperator.description:
The operator vocabulary a `FactorField` accepts — mirrors `schemas.screener.
ScreenerOperator` but scoped to what the condition builder's `FilterValueInput` renders.
FactorOperator.title: FactorOperator

FactorScore.description:
One factor's contribution to the composite. `percentile is None` means the factor is
genuinely unavailable for this symbol/date (its source dataset isn't ingested yet, or
there isn't enough history) — it is never defaulted to a fake neutral value that would
silently bias the blend.
FactorScore.title: FactorScore

FearGreedIndexRow.description:
`fear_greed_index` — one day's CNN Fear & Greed Index reading (US equity-market
sentiment gauge). Backer/Sponsor-only; market-level, no symbol scope. Modeled `Market.US` —
the index is specifically a US-market sentiment gauge, a genuine single-country home.
FearGreedIndexRow.title: FearGreedIndexRow

FeedbackRecord.description: The persisted outcome of a feedback submission — enough for the route to echo back.
FeedbackRecord.title: FeedbackRecord

FieldDef.description:
One channel's mapping to a data field — never a value, always a field NAME the renderer
looks up per-row.
FieldDef.title: FieldDef

FieldType.description:
The four Vega-Lite field types this grammar needs — drives axis/scale choice and the
mark-compatibility rules below.
FieldType.title: FieldType

FinMindInternationalMarket.description:
The four non-TW markets FinMind carries its own roster+price datasets for — distinct
from the full `schemas.enums.Market` set (HK/GLOBAL have no FinMind international dataset).
FinMindInternationalMarket.title: FinMindInternationalMarket

FinancialStatementLine.description:
`financials` — one line item from an income/balance/cash-flow statement. `period_type`
defaults to `"quarterly"` — FinMind (TW's source for this capability) reports one frequency
only, so every existing TW row is implicitly quarterly; yfinance (the US/non-TW source)
reports annual/quarterly/TTM as genuinely distinct frames, so US rows set this field for
real rather than leaving every US row ambiguously defaulted.
FinancialStatementLine.title: FinancialStatementLine

ForeignShareholdingRow.description: `foreign_shareholding` — one day's 外資持股 (foreign shareholding) row for one stock.
ForeignShareholdingRow.title: ForeignShareholdingRow

FundComparisonRow.description:
One requested symbol's total-return + basic-profile slice.

`total_return_pct` is computed with dividends reinvested at the ex-dividend date's close
(see module docstring for the exact convention/approximation) — `None` only when price
history itself is unusable (never fabricated).

unavailable_note.description: Honest reason a field (overlap%/premium-discount/NAV) is absent for this row, e.g. the TW-holdings-gap note — never a silently-missing field.
unavailable_note.title: Unavailable Note

FundComparisonRow.title: FundComparisonRow

FundHoldingRow.description:
`fund_holdings` — one top-holding constituent row of one ETF/mutual fund
(`yfinance.scrapers.funds.FundsData.top_holdings`). Distinct from `etf_holdings`
(issuer-PCF-sourced, TW-scoped, fund-level metadata only) — this is yfinance's own
holdings-weight slice, relevant for non-TW ETFs.
FundHoldingRow.title: FundHoldingRow

FundProfileRow.description:
`fund_profile` — one non-TW ETF/mutual fund's identity + summary-return fields from
yfinance's own `.info` payload (`sources/yfinance/analyst.py::_fund_profile`). The 總覽
tab's fund-equivalent of `GetCompanyProfileOutput` for a plain equity — a fund has no
chairman/EPS/capital, but has real AUM/category/issuer/return figures `ProfileCard` never
surfaced. Every field degrades to `None` independently (never fabricated) when yfinance's
own `.info` payload doesn't carry it for this symbol.
FundProfileRow.title: FundProfileRow

FundSectorWeightingRow.description:
`fund_holdings` (sector-weighting slice) — one sector-weight row for one ETF/mutual
fund (`FundsData.sector_weightings`).
FundSectorWeightingRow.title: FundSectorWeightingRow

FuturesDailyRow.description: `futures_daily` — one day's futures contract EOD price/volume row.
FuturesDailyRow.title: FuturesDailyRow

FuturesInstitutionalFlowRow.description:
`futures_institutional_flow` — one day's three-major-institutional-investor futures
buy/sell + open-interest-balance row. The upstream columns for this dataset do not include a
per-contract identifier, so on a whole-market (omit-`data_id`) call `symbol` reads empty —
a documented upstream gap, not a mapper defect.
FuturesInstitutionalFlowRow.title: FuturesInstitutionalFlowRow

FuturesOiLargeTradersRow.description:
`futures_oi_large_traders` — one day's 大額交易人未沖銷部位 (large-trader open-interest
concentration) row for one futures contract type. Backer/Sponsor-only.

Bundles earnings/IPO/economic calendars into one report — a distinct, narrower
yfinance-native feed bundle than a possible future `get_calendar_events` analytics-layer

GetCanonicalContextOutput.title: GetCanonicalContextOutput

GetChipFlowsOutput.description:

unentitled caller (`supports_row_preview=True` — governance.md §4 top-N-preview exception);
`run()` itself is what nulls `buy_top`/`sell_top` rows beyond `free_row_count` and empties
`rows`/`top_brokers` for that caller — `dispatch_tool` never inspects this output's fields.
GetChipFlowsOutput.title: GetChipFlowsOutput

GetCompanyProfileOutput.description:
A company-profile card composed from every capability wired below: `sector_class`
(industry/sector), `dividends` (latest announced dividend), `market_value`/
`valuation_ratios` (市值/PER/殖利率), `financials` (EPS, from the income-statement lines),
`profile` (MOPS-sourced identity fields — 董事長/簽證會計師/住址/官網/資本額/發言人/成立日期/
產業別), and two derived-store reads: `revenue_yoy` (this month's filed revenue vs the same
calendar month a year prior, from the ingested `TaiwanStockMonthRevenue` dataset) and
`margins` (TTM gross profit ÷ TTM revenue, from the same ingested statement lines `eps`
reads — see `analytics/fundamentals.py`). Each field is only ever populated from a genuinely
healthy fetch/read for this call; `missing_fields` is computed per-call from which fetches
actually succeeded, never a static reduced list, so the agent never claims completeness it
doesn't have.

missing_fields.description: Fields this profile call could not populate — either no adapter exists for that capability, or this call's fetch of it was unhealthy/empty. Never silently omitted from the caller.
missing_fields.title: Missing Fields

GetCompanyProfileOutput.title: GetCompanyProfileOutput

GetDividendPolicySummaryOutput.description:
A composite report bundling everything the 股利政策 card needs — the announced-schedule
events (table rows), the per-year chart bars, the stats-strip figures, and the per-event
fill results — in one call, rather than the frontend fanning out to `get_dividend_schedule`
+ `get_financial_statement` + a long-range price fetch and re-deriving payout/fill-rate
itself. Mirrors `GetCorporateActionEventsOutput`'s bundling precedent (multiple capability
fetches, one composite tool) and `MonthRevenueTrendPoint`'s "pre-compute, cite directly"
convention.

aum_caveat.default: 資產規模 (AUM) is Yahoo's own totalAssets figure for this fund — refreshed weekly, not a live figure; may be missing for a recently-listed or thinly-covered fund.

distribution_caveat.default: 配息率/頻率 are inferred from the trailing-12-month cadence of real cash-distribution events — an observed-cadence classification, not the issuer's declared distribution policy, and approximate for a fund listed under 12 months.

unavailable_symbols.description: Requested symbols whose FUND_HOLDINGS fetch degraded (no usable holdings data) — named honestly here, never silently dropped from the request.

GetEtfPremiumDiscountOutput.description:
`etf_nav` (+ `etf_aum`) read for one ETF: TWSE's own published 預估折溢價幅度 history —

`job_etf_nav`). `current_aum` is folded in from the separate `etf_aum` dataset rather than

methodology_note.default: Total return assumes each cash dividend is reinvested at that ex-dividend date's closing price — a standard approximation, not an account-level simulation of actual reinvestment timing or fees.

contribution_caveat.default: Estimated from market-cap weight x price change; not TWSE's official float-adjusted index-contribution figure — this codebase has no float-adjusted-divisor data.

GetPriceQuoteOutput.description: The basic price-quote read (part of the immediate-core set).
GetPriceQuoteOutput.title: GetPriceQuoteOutput

describe the peer-list fetch specifically (the caveat that actually matters to a reader of

GetStockScoreOutput.description:

honest `found=False` with a plain-language reason when it has not (never a fabricated or

GetStockSummaryOutput.description:
The detail-page read: the AI-generated headline/narrative/SWOT grounded in today's cached
composite score, or an honest `found=False` when no score exists yet to ground it in (never

GetSupplyChainEdgesOutput.description:
Every published supply-chain edge where the company is either endpoint — the 供應鏈關係圖
card's one data source. `edges` carries both directions; each edge's `from_symbol`/`to_symbol`
(with `from_market`/`to_market`) disambiguates. Only verified, non-stale relations appear
(candidates, rejected and stale rows are hidden). Each edge states its `grade`
(`confidence` is the legacy name for the same value), product, as-of date and source links.
Empty, not an error, for a company with no published relations.

GetSymbolDirectorySearchOutput.description:
Same "absent, never fabricated" contract as `GetSymbolInfoOutput` — an empty `rows` means
no roster match, not a placeholder result.

GetSymbolInfoOutput.description:
One row per symbol that exists in the latest ingested roster — a symbol not found there
(delisted, mistyped, or not yet in an ETF/warrant roster this dataset covers) is simply
absent from `rows`, never a fabricated placeholder name.

GetSymbolThemesOutput.description:
The reverse lookup — every theme a symbol belongs to, with that membership's own
sub-industry and confidence.
GetSymbolThemesOutput.title: GetSymbolThemesOutput

non_trading_caveat.default: 技術指標與型態為圖表描述，非買賣建議 — indicators/patterns describe the chart, they are not a trading instruction.

GetThemeMembersOutput.description:
A theme's identity plus its member symbols, each carrying the per-membership
`sub_industry`/`confidence`/`source` so an AI-researched concept member is never presented as

GetThemeTierHeatmapOutput.description:
A theme's upstream/midstream/downstream sub-industry tiles, each colored by its own

tier assignment carries its `source` (curated editorial map vs keyword heuristic) so a caller
can tell an editorially-verified position from an automatically-classified one and never
present a heuristic guess as equally authoritative.

GetTrendScoreOutput.description:

GoldPriceRow.description:
`gold_price` — one day's gold spot-price reading. Free tier; market-level, no symbol
scope. Modeled `Market.GLOBAL` — a world commodity benchmark, no single-country home.
GoldPriceRow.title: GoldPriceRow

GovernmentBankBuySellRow.description:
`government_bank_buysell` — one day's 八大行庫 (eight state-owned/government banks)
buy/sell row for one stock. Sponsor-only.
GovernmentBankBuySellRow.title: GovernmentBankBuySellRow

GovernmentBondYieldRow.description:
`government_bond_yield` — one day's US Treasury yield reading for one maturity tenor
(`symbol` e.g. "United States 10-Year"). Free tier. Modeled `Market.US` — unlike
`central_bank_rate`, this dataset's underlying is specifically the US Treasury curve, a
genuine single-country home.
GovernmentBondYieldRow.title: GovernmentBondYieldRow

HolderAccumulationRow.description:
`locked=True` rows (governance.md §4 top-N-preview exception) have every field but
`rank` nulled server-side — an unentitled caller must not learn which stock a locked row
even names.
HolderAccumulationRow.title: HolderAccumulationRow

HoldingStatus.description:
The derived per-holding classification layered on top of FinMind's raw buy/sell change
row — never stored by FinMind itself, computed here from (buy, sell, prior-day weight).
HoldingStatus.title: HoldingStatus

IndexContributionRow.description:
`locked=True` rows (governance.md §4 top-N-preview exception) have every field but `rank`
nulled server-side.
IndexContributionRow.title: IndexContributionRow

IndustryChainMoneyFlowRow.description:
`industry_chain_money_flow` — one day's 產業鏈資金流向 (industry-chain money-flow)
aggregate row for one industry (or sub-industry). Sponsor-only; market-level, no symbol
scope. `sub_industry` empty means an industry-chain total row — these do NOT equal the sum
of that chain's sub-industry rows (a stock can belong to multiple sub-industries), and a
stock can belong to multiple chains, so `trading_money_pct` across chains sums to more than
100%.

`locked=True` rows (governance.md §4 top-N-preview exception) have every field but `rank`/
`market`/`trade_date`/`is_total` nulled server-side — `sub_industry` itself is nulled, so
`is_total` (not `sub_industry == ""`) is how a caller/renderer tells a locked chain-total
row from a locked sub-industry breakdown row.
IndustryChainMoneyFlowRow.title: IndustryChainMoneyFlowRow

IndustryOverviewCompanyRow.description:
`industry_overview` — one top-company row within one `yfinance.Industry` aggregate
view (analogous to `sector_overview`, one level narrower).

`ytd_return`/`last_price`/`target_price` come from `yfinance.Industry.top_performing_
companies` (only populated on a `row_kind="performing_company"` row); `ytd_return`/
`growth_estimate` come from `top_growth_companies` (`row_kind="growth_company"` only). A
plain `row_kind="company"` row (from `top_companies`, the same frame `sector_overview` reads)
never carries any of these four — left `None`, never fabricated from the other frames.
IndustryOverviewCompanyRow.title: IndustryOverviewCompanyRow

InsiderActivityRow.description:
`insider_activity` — one insider (Form-4-derived) transaction row. US-style disclosure;
sparse/empty for non-US markets — never fabricated when absent.
InsiderActivityRow.title: InsiderActivityRow

InsiderTransferDeclarationRow.description:
`insider_transfer_declaration` — one 內部人股權轉讓事前申報 (insider advance-transfer-plan
declaration) row from TWSE MOPS's `t187ap12_L` whole-market dump. Advance notice of an
intended insider share transfer/sale, filed before it happens — distinct from
`DirectorShareholding` (a monthly holdings snapshot, not an event) and from
`Capability.INSIDER_ACTIVITY` (yfinance/US Form-4-derived, never TW).

Scoped to `t187ap12_L` only. `t187ap13_L` (a related but distinct "reason not transferred"
filing) is intentionally not covered by this model — a real, separate MOPS dataset, deferred
rather than silently dropped.
InsiderTransferDeclarationRow.title: InsiderTransferDeclarationRow

InstitutionalFlowRollingNet.description:
One investor category's pre-summed net buy/sell (`sum(buy - sell)`) over the trailing
5/10/20-trading-day windows within whatever range `get_institutional_flow` fetched — see
that tool's own docstring for why this exists: without it, a skill asking for a "5/10/20
日買賣超趨勢" forces the model to sum 20+ raw daily rows by hand across every investor
category, which measurably happened live (a `chip-flow-review` turn's reasoning trace
showed it manually adding up 20 days x 3 categories and running out of response budget
before writing any prose at all — the final answer had zero analysis, just a raw table).
A window field is `None` when fewer trading days than that window exist in the fetched
range (e.g. a 5-day request can't back a 20-day figure) — never a partial-window number
silently mislabeled as the full window.
InstitutionalFlowRollingNet.title: InstitutionalFlowRollingNet

InstitutionalFlowRow.description: `institutional_flow` — one institutional-investor buy/sell row for one trading day.
InstitutionalFlowRow.title: InstitutionalFlowRow

InstitutionalFlowTotalMarketRow.description:
`institutional_flow_total_market` — one day's whole-market three-major-institutional-
investor buy/sell total row for one category (`name`). Market-level, no symbol scope.
InstitutionalFlowTotalMarketRow.title: InstitutionalFlowTotalMarketRow

InstitutionalHolderRow.description:
`institutional_holders` — one institutional or mutual-fund holder row (US-style 13F-
derived disclosure; `holder_type` distinguishes the two source tables).
InstitutionalHolderRow.title: InstitutionalHolderRow

InstitutionalStreak.description: An institutional investor class net bought/sold for `days` consecutive trading days.
InstitutionalStreak.title: InstitutionalStreak

InternationalStockInfoRow.description:
`us_stock_info` / `uk_stock_info` / `europe_stock_info` / `japan_stock_info` — one roster
row of a non-Taiwan market's stock universe reference table. Free tier. `region_detail`
carries whatever region/exchange/sector column that market's dataset documents (US: Country;
UK: Country; Europe: Market; Japan: Exchange) — kept as one free-text field rather than four
diverging optional columns, since none of the four datasets share a common taxonomy for it.
InternationalStockInfoRow.title: InternationalStockInfoRow

InternationalStockPriceRow.description:
`us_stock_price` / `uk_stock_price` / `europe_stock_price` / `japan_stock_price` — one
day's EOD bar for a non-Taiwan market stock. Free tier. `data_id` for these datasets is the
market's own quote symbol (e.g. `^DJI`, `BP.L`, `AALB.AS`, `7203.T`), never a Taiwan-style
numeric `stock_id` — passed straight through as `symbol`, not reparsed.
InternationalStockPriceRow.title: InternationalStockPriceRow

KBarRow.description:
`intraday_kbar` — one minute-bar for one stock. Sponsor-only; single trading day per
request upstream.
KBarRow.title: KBarRow

KdResult.description:
Stochastic oscillator %K / %D. Both series are `None` for `i` inside the warm-up window
(fewer than `period` bars seen yet) — never a fabricated number standing in for "not enough
history". `k`/`d` share the same length and warm-up prefix.
KdResult.title: KdResult

LivePriceTick.description:
One decoded `PricingData` WebSocket message — mapped straight off yfinance's own
snake_case field names (`MessageToDict(..., preserving_proto_field_name=True)`).
LivePriceTick.title: LivePriceTick

LiveQuoteSnapshot.description: One TWSE MIS best-5 bid/ask + last-trade snapshot row.
LiveQuoteSnapshot.title: LiveQuoteSnapshot

LlmUsageSummary.description:
What the usage settings page draws: a dense daily series (zero-filled, oldest first),
per-model totals (largest first) and the grand total for the window.
LlmUsageSummary.title: LlmUsageSummary

MacroReleaseEventRow.description:
`macro_calendar` — one upcoming/recent macro-release event row
(`financecalendar.com`'s `wp-json/fc/v1/calendar` feed, a distinct third-party source from
`EconomicCalendarRow`'s yfinance `Calendars` feed — see `sources/financecalendar.py`'s own
module docstring for why this is additive, not a replacement). Modeled `Market.GLOBAL`: the
feed spans multiple countries (US GDP/CPI/NFP, RBA/ECB/BOJ rate decisions, Australia/Canada/
Eurozone releases, ...), distinguished only by the free-text `category`/`name` fields, the
same "no single-country home" reasoning `EconomicCalendarRow` already uses.

`consensus`/`prior`/`actual` are deliberately `str | None`, never `float` — the live upstream
returns human-readable strings ("Hold at 3.50-3.75%", "3.8% annual", "55.6") that mix ranges,
units, and plain numbers; coercing them to a float would either fail or silently misrepresent
a range/unit. Render as opaque cited text, never parsed or computed on.
MacroReleaseEventRow.title: MacroReleaseEventRow

MacroUnits.description: The upstream `units` transformation codes the catalog uses (stored per series).
MacroUnits.title: MacroUnits

MarginBalanceChange.description:
融資 (margin purchase) or 融券 (short sale) balance moved by a percentage in one day,
computed from the row's own today-vs-yesterday balances.
MarginBalanceChange.title: MarginBalanceChange

MarginMaintenanceRatioRow.description:
`margin_maintenance_ratio` — one day's whole-market 融資維持率 (margin maintenance ratio)
reading. Backer/Sponsor-only; market-level, no symbol scope.
MarginMaintenanceRatioRow.title: MarginMaintenanceRatioRow

MarginShortRow.description:
`margin_short` — one day's 融資融劵 (margin purchase / short sale) balance row for one
stock.
MarginShortRow.title: MarginShortRow

MarginShortTotalMarketRow.description:
`margin_short_total_market` — one day's whole-market margin/short-sale total row for one
category (`name`, e.g. TWSE/TPEx). Market-level, no symbol scope.
MarginShortTotalMarketRow.title: MarginShortTotalMarketRow

Mark.description:
The 5 chart shapes this grammar covers. Waterfall/range-bar is `BAR` + `y2`, not a
separate mark (see `ChartHint.y2`'s own docstring) — kept at 5 rather than 6 marks.
Mark.title: Mark

Market.description: Drives routing, calendar rules, currency, timezone. Add by config.
Market.title: Market

MarketIndexStripItemRow.description:
`market_index_strip` — one item in the TW-tab ticker strip
(加權指數/櫃買指數/美元/黃金/原油). Free tier only — every underlying dataset this row draws
from (`TAIEX_5S_INDEX`/`TOTAL_RETURN_INDEX`/`EXCHANGE_RATE`/`GOLD_PRICE`/`CRUDE_OIL_PRICES`)
is already `DataClass.PUBLIC` at its own dataset declaration; this row never represents a
Sponsor-tier reading (those render through their own existing tools — `get_tick_snapshot`/
`get_futures_snapshot`/`get_taiex_vix` — masked like any other Sponsor card, not folded into
this bundle). `change`/`change_pct` are `None` when only one day's reading is available (no
prior day to diff against), never a fabricated zero.
MarketIndexStripItemRow.title: MarketIndexStripItemRow

MarketRankingRow.description:
One ranked row — the exact column set the 排行榜 reference design shows (名稱/代號, 最新價,
漲跌, 漲跌幅, 成交量). Every field is read straight from `ScreenerHit.matched_fields`
(Yahoo's own raw quote fields, already a passthrough dict — see `sources/yfinance/
screener.py::_quote_to_hit`), never a separate fetch.
MarketRankingRow.title: MarketRankingRow

MaskedTeaser.description:
The masked-teaser envelope for an unentitled `sponsor` call — rendered blurred/馬賽克
with an upgrade CTA by the frontend. Never a hard error/exception; this is a normal,
successful tool result shape.
MaskedTeaser.title: MaskedTeaser

MaterialAnnouncement.description:
`corporate_actions` — one 重大訊息 (material announcement) disclosure row. Third-party
regulatory-filing content: `subject`/`detail` remain free Chinese text (that is the actual
content of the filing), never summarized or translated into a trading signal.
MaterialAnnouncement.title: MaterialAnnouncement

MaterialAnnouncementPublished.description:
The company filed a 重大訊息 (material announcement) with the exchange. An event, not a
state: it says a filing exists - the notification quotes the filer's own subject line as data,
and never characterises it.
MaterialAnnouncementPublished.title: MaterialAnnouncementPublished

MaterialAnnouncementRow.description:
`corporate_actions` — one 重大訊息 row from the WHOLE-MARKET dump (ingest-owned, one
partition per day), distinct from `MaterialAnnouncement` (the per-symbol live-fetch shape
`get_material_announcements` still serves). `category` is a derived bucket computed at
ingest time (`sources/mops.py::_announcement_category`) from `qualifying_clause` — TWSE's own
disclosure-rule clause citation (e.g. "第51款"), meaningless to a reader as a raw number, so
never exposed un-bucketed to a whole-market list view. `qualifying_clause` itself is kept
alongside `category` rather than dropped, for anyone who wants the raw citation.
MaterialAnnouncementRow.title: MaterialAnnouncementRow

Memory.description:
One long-term memory record — `memories` row shape.

`type=MemoryType.WATCHLIST` may only appear when constructing a `Memory` from an existing
legacy row (`memory.store.MemoryStore` never sets it on a new write); this model itself
does not enforce that distinction — see `memory/store.py`'s `upsert` for the write-path
gate — because a *read* path (listing legacy rows) legitimately needs to construct one.
Memory.title: Memory

MemoryRef.description:
A long-term memory that informed this turn - shown to the user under the answer. `text` is
a short snippet (the memory is the user's own), enough to recognise it.
MemoryRef.title: MemoryRef

MemoryType.description:
`WATCHLIST` is retained only so legacy rows written before the relational watchlist
store existed still validate — `memory.store.MemoryStore.upsert` refuses to write a new
one (see that module's docstring).
MemoryType.title: MemoryType

Message.description:
One node in a turn's message tree. `parent_id=None` marks a root message. Only the
chain from the thread's `active_leaf_message_id` back to its root is ever sent to the
LLM — see `conversation.store.ConversationStore.active_path`.
Message.title: Message

ModelUsage.description:
One turn's LLM consumption on a single (provider, model) - what the usage settings chart
is built from. `cost_micros` is only filled where the provider reports a charge inline
(OpenRouter); it is 0, not an estimate, everywhere else.
ModelUsage.title: ModelUsage

MonthRevenuePublished.description: The symbol's monthly-revenue (月營收) figure has been published.
MonthRevenuePublished.title: MonthRevenuePublished

MonthRevenueRow.description: `month_revenue` — one 月營收 (monthly revenue) filing row for one stock.
MonthRevenueRow.title: MonthRevenueRow

MonthRevenueTrendPoint.description:
One filed month's revenue plus its pre-computed MoM/YoY change, cumulative-YoY, a
same-calendar-month record flag, and (when available) that month's period-end closing price
— so a skill asking for a "近期月營收趨勢" never forces the model to manually diff adjacent
rows itself (the same failure class as `InstitutionalFlowRollingNet`: a live
`earnings-quality` turn's reasoning trace showed the model hand-transcribing raw
month-revenue rows into a markdown table and running out of response budget before writing
any prose — the final answer had zero analysis). `mom_pct`/`yoy_pct`/`cumulative_yoy_pct` are
`None` when the comparison month(s) are absent from `rows`, never a fabricated figure from a
mismatched month. `period_end_close` is `None` when no `PRICE_EOD` bar exists on or before
this month's last filed trading day (e.g. a symbol whose price history doesn't reach this far
back) — never fabricated as an interpolated/estimated price.
MonthRevenueTrendPoint.title: MonthRevenueTrendPoint

MovingAverageBundle.description:
MA5/10/20/60/120/240 together — 均線排列 (the moving-average stack) is read as a set, not
one line at a time. MA120/240 were added for the K線 chart's overlay chips; the score/screener
callers that predate them only ever read `ma5..ma60`, so their existing behavior is
unaffected.
MovingAverageBundle.title: MovingAverageBundle

Notification.description:
One delivered (or in-app persisted) notification record. `dedupe_key` encodes
`(source_id, trigger_date, channel)`; `(user_id, dedupe_key)` is unique, which is what makes
redelivery a no-op under at-least-once execution.
Notification.title: Notification

NotificationBadge.description: The lightweight counts the mobile tab-island + top-bar bell dots read.
NotificationBadge.title: NotificationBadge

OptionContractRow.description: `options_chain` — one option contract row (one strike, one side) for one expiry.
OptionContractRow.title: OptionContractRow

OptionDailyRow.description: `option_daily` — one day's option contract EOD price/volume row.
OptionDailyRow.title: OptionDailyRow

OptionInstitutionalFlowRow.description:
`option_institutional_flow` — one day's three-major-institutional-investor option
buy/sell + open-interest-balance row, split by `call_put`. The upstream columns for this
dataset do not include a per-contract identifier, so on a whole-market (omit-`data_id`) call
`symbol` reads empty — a documented upstream gap, not a mapper defect.
OptionInstitutionalFlowRow.title: OptionInstitutionalFlowRow

OptionOiLargeTradersRow.description:
`option_oi_large_traders` — one day's 大額交易人未沖銷部位 (large-trader open-interest
concentration) row for one option contract type, split by `put_call`. Backer/Sponsor-only.

buy_top10_specific_open_interest_per.title: Buy Top10 Specific Open Interest Per

buy_top10_trader_open_interest_per.title: Buy Top10 Trader Open Interest Per

buy_top5_specific_open_interest_per.title: Buy Top5 Specific Open Interest Per

buy_top5_trader_open_interest_per.title: Buy Top5 Trader Open Interest Per

sell_top10_specific_open_interest_per.title: Sell Top10 Specific Open Interest Per

sell_top10_trader_open_interest_per.title: Sell Top10 Trader Open Interest Per

sell_top5_specific_open_interest_per.title: Sell Top5 Specific Open Interest Per

sell_top5_trader_open_interest_per.title: Sell Top5 Trader Open Interest Per

OptionOiLargeTradersRow.title: OptionOiLargeTradersRow

OptionVixRow.description:
`option_vix` — one 臺指選擇權波動率指數 (TAIEX option volatility index) reading.
Backer/Sponsor-only; market-level, no symbol scope.
OptionVixRow.title: OptionVixRow

OrderBookStatsRow.description:
`order_book_stats` — one 5-second whole-exchange order-book/trade aggregate. Market-level,
no symbol scope; single trading day per request upstream.
OrderBookStatsRow.title: OrderBookStatsRow

OverlapHoldingRow.description:
One holding present in 2+ of the requested ETFs — the row shape the "which ETFs hold
this, at what weight" view needs.
OverlapHoldingRow.title: OverlapHoldingRow

OwnedPet.description: One `user_pets` row — an owned, possibly-equipped pet.
OwnedPet.title: OwnedPet

PairOverlapRow.description:
One (etf_a, etf_b) pair's overlap percentage — sum of `min(weight_in_a, weight_in_b)`
over every holding both hold (see module docstring for why this convention was chosen).
PairOverlapRow.title: PairOverlapRow

PersonalityPresetView.description:
What the Settings picker needs to show a preset. The preset's prompt `fragment` stays on the
server: it is governance-reviewed system-prompt text, not something a client needs.
PersonalityPresetView.title: PersonalityPresetView

PetCatalogEntry.description:
One catalog pet definition. Bilingual, TW/finance flavor lives only in name/description
— never in mechanics.
PetCatalogEntry.title: PetCatalogEntry

PetProgress.description:
The stats row plus the code-defined completion/milestone/pity context the UI renders.

`pity_rare_at`/`pity_legendary_at`/`level_milestones` are the raw configured thresholds
`pets.config` already defines (`PITY_RARE_AT`/`PITY_LEGENDARY_AT`/`LEVEL_MILESTONE_PULLS`) —
reporting them here is what lets a client show "N pulls to guaranteed rare" or "next
milestone at level M" against the stats this same response already carries (`pity_counter`
for the pity math; the *equipped* pet's own `level`, from `GET /pets/active`, for the
milestone math) without hardcoding those thresholds client-side.
PetProgress.title: PetProgress

PetSettings.description:
`hint_enabled`: may the equipped pet flavour replies? Off until the user opts in.
`companion_visible`: show the avatar and its notices in chat (on by default).
PetSettings.title: PetSettings

PlanPrice.description: A price as Paddle states it: `amount` in the currency's minor units (a string).
PlanPrice.title: PlanPrice

PresetCondition.description:
One condition inside a preset — the same shape `run_screener` accepts, minus the `market`
wrapper (a preset is scoped to one market by construction).
PresetCondition.title: PresetCondition

PriceLimitRow.description:
`price_limit` — one day's reference/limit-up/limit-down price row for one stock.
`limit_up`/`limit_down` of 0 means no price-change limit applies (leveraged/inverse ETFs,
emerging-board stocks).
PriceLimitRow.title: PriceLimitRow

PriceTickRow.description:
`price_tick` — one tick-level trade record. Backer/Sponsor-only; single trading day per
request upstream.
PriceTickRow.title: PriceTickRow

PullOutcome.description: The result of a gacha pull — either a newly obtained pet or a duplicate converted to XP.
PullOutcome.title: PullOutcome

PutStrategySubscriptionRequest.description:
The whole subscription. Empty `channels` / null `quiet_hours` inherit the user's alert
preferences; null `watchlist_id` means every stock on today's screen. `expected_version` is the
version the client last saw (409 when it changed meanwhile); omit it to create.
PutStrategySubscriptionRequest.title: PutStrategySubscriptionRequest

QuietHours.description:
A per-user quiet window, stored as ISO `HH:MM` strings (portable — no DB `time` type
reliance across dialects). A window that wraps past midnight (start > end) is honoured.
QuietHours.title: QuietHours

RankingKind.description:
One tab of the 排行榜 card. `TRENDING` is Yahoo's own named screen (no sort field of our
own choosing); every other kind is a custom query sorted by the matching Yahoo screener
field — see each's own `_SORT_FIELD_BY_KIND`/`_CURRENCY_FILTERED_KINDS` entry below.
RankingKind.title: RankingKind

RevokeTokenResponse.description: RFC 7009 answers with an empty JSON object.
RevokeTokenResponse.title: RevokeTokenResponse

degraded.description: Human-readable notes on any condition this pass could not evaluate (e.g. an unknown factor key) — never silently dropped.
degraded.title: Degraded

ScheduleAction.description:
What a job runs: a governed skill by name plus its inputs. The skill is resolved against
the same `SkillRegistry` interactive turns use — a scheduled run reuses a governed skill,
never a bespoke code path.
ScheduleAction.title: ScheduleAction

ScoreBand.description:
A descriptive label of what the current factor mix shows — never an instruction. No
band value may ever be a buy/sell/hold word; this enum is the single place that mapping is
defined, so it can't drift per call site.
ScoreBand.title: ScoreBand

ScoreProfile.description: Which of the two horizon-aware weight profiles produced this score.
ScoreProfile.title: ScoreProfile

ScoreResult.description:
The composite's full, transparent output: the number, the band, and the factor
breakdown behind it — the number is never surfaced without its basis (governance's "show
the work" rule). Nothing here is, or may become, buy/sell/hold/price-target/position-sizing
language.

`breakdown` is `StockScoreBreakdown` for a plain equity, `EtfScoreBreakdown` for any ETF
(plain/active/leveraged/inverse) — the two shapes have different factor names by design
(see each breakdown's own docstring for why the factor sets genuinely differ, not just a
naming variation). Callers branch on `isinstance(result.breakdown, EtfScoreBreakdown)` (or
check `symbol_type`) rather than assuming one fixed shape.

normalization_caveat.description: How the cross-sectional factors were standardized — in particular whether value/quality were compared against sector peers or, absent an ingested sector classification, the whole universe (disclosed, never silently presented as sector-relative).
normalization_caveat.title: Normalization Caveat

partial_factors.description: Names of factors that were unavailable and excluded from the composite — disclosed explicitly, never a silent degradation.
partial_factors.title: Partial Factors

ScoreResult.title: ScoreResult

ScreenerOperator.description:
`gt/gte/lt/lte/eq` are single-value comparisons; `between` takes `value`+`value2`
(inclusive range); `in` takes `values` (membership test against an enum-like field, e.g.
sector/region).
ScreenerOperator.title: ScreenerOperator

ScreenerPreset.description:
One named preset: a category, bilingual labels, a one-line description, a directional cue
(`bull`/`bear`/`neutral`, drives the card's left-edge bar per README.md §3), and the condition
set + match mode it loads into the builder.
ScreenerPreset.title: ScreenerPreset

ScreenerRunRequest.description:
The `POST /analytics/screener/run` body — a JSON object rather than query params, since
`conditions[]`/`gate_overrides` are nested structures that don't flatten trivially into a
GET query string (same reasoning `market_rest.py`'s `_split_symbols` docstring gives for
other nested-shape routes, but here the nesting is deep enough that even a flattened
repeated-key encoding would be awkward, so this route is a plain POST instead).
ScreenerRunRequest.title: ScreenerRunRequest

ScreenerSurvivor.description:
One row surviving gates+setup. `matched_conditions` names which requested conditions this
symbol satisfied (AND: all of them; OR: the satisfied subset) — same "show the work"
transparency rule `TagScreenerHit.matched_tags` already uses.

`display` carries a small set of already-fetched quote fields for the results table to
render without a second per-symbol lookup — populated only for US (Yahoo's screener response
already includes `regularMarketPrice`/`marketCap`/etc. for every hit; TW/ETF survivors get
their price/volume/sector from the existing `useSymbolQuotes` batched read instead, so this
stays empty for those markets rather than duplicating that path).
ScreenerSurvivor.title: ScreenerSurvivor

SecFiling.description:
`sec_filings` — one SEC EDGAR filing row for a listed US company (yfinance's
`Ticker.get_sec_filings()`). Third-party regulatory-filing content: `title`/`type` are the
filing's own metadata, never summarized into a trading signal. US-only — no equivalent feed
exists for any other market this codebase serves.
SecFiling.title: SecFiling

SecretKind.description: `user_secrets.kind` vocabulary. `LLM_KEY` is the BYOK case that lifts the chat limit.
SecretKind.title: SecretKind

SectorConstituentRow.description:
One stock within a `get_sector_heatmap` industry tile — the per-symbol breakdown a
treemap drill-down needs, which `SectorHeatmapRow` itself deliberately only aggregates.
SectorConstituentRow.title: SectorConstituentRow

SectorHeatmapRow.description:
One industry's aggregate tile — colored by `avg_pct_change`, sized by `stock_count` (or
`total_turnover`, when trading-value weighting was available for this industry).
SectorHeatmapRow.title: SectorHeatmapRow

SectorIndustryWeightRow.description:
One row of `yfinance.Sector.industries` — this sector's own industry breakdown by market
weight (e.g. Technology -> Semiconductors 38%, Software-Infrastructure 21%, ...). The data
source for a sector-industries composition treemap; distinct from `IndustryOverviewCompanyRow`
(a company within ONE industry) — this is industries within ONE sector.
SectorIndustryWeightRow.title: SectorIndustryWeightRow

SectorOverviewCompanyRow.description:
`sector_overview` — one top-company/top-ETF/top-mutual-fund row within one
`yfinance.Sector` aggregate view. `row_kind` distinguishes the three sub-lists this
capability folds together rather than splitting into three near-duplicate capabilities.
SectorOverviewCompanyRow.title: SectorOverviewCompanyRow

SectorOverviewStats.description:
`sector_overview`'s aggregate-level stats — `yfinance.Sector.overview`'s own dict, mapped
1:1. Distinct from `SectorOverviewCompanyRow` (a per-company row): this is the ONE summary
for the whole sector aggregate itself, not a company within it.
SectorOverviewStats.title: SectorOverviewStats

SectorRotationDayRow.description:
One industry's rank + net institutional flow for one trading day within the rotation
window.
SectorRotationDayRow.title: SectorRotationDayRow

SectorRrgSeries.description: One industry sub-index's full RRG history — a trail `CometTail`/`RankPanel` renders.
SectorRrgSeries.title: SectorRrgSeries

SectorRrgWeekPoint.description:
One industry's RS-Ratio/RS-Momentum reading for one ISO week — the JdK relative-rotation
coordinate pair `RotationCanvas` plots per sector per week.
SectorRrgWeekPoint.title: SectorRrgWeekPoint

SecuritiesLendingRow.description: `securities_lending` — one 借券成交 (securities-lending transaction) row for one stock.
SecuritiesLendingRow.title: SecuritiesLendingRow

ShareholdingDistributionRow.description:
`shareholding_distribution` — one 股權持股分級表 (shareholding-level distribution) row for
one stock. Backer/Sponsor-only.
ShareholdingDistributionRow.title: ShareholdingDistributionRow

SignalTag.description:
One boolean 訊號 tag, the catalog's copy of a `TagDefinition` (see `catalog.py`) reshaped
for the condition builder's Signals sub-mode — a checklist item, not a slider row.
SignalTag.title: SignalTag

SmaResult.description:
Simple moving average. `values[i] is None` for `i` inside the warm-up window (fewer
than `window` bars seen yet) — never a fabricated number standing in for "not enough
history".
SmaResult.title: SmaResult

SourceHealthEntryOut.description:
One capability's currentness/closure diagnostic — mirrors `SourceHealthEntry` without
re-exporting `context/`'s own model as a tool output type.
SourceHealthEntryOut.title: SourceHealthEntryOut

SpeakResponse.description:
The synthesized audio, base64-encoded for a JSON envelope. `spoken_text` is the exact
caveated text that was voiced — the caveat is guaranteed present by `voice.service.speak`.
SpeakResponse.title: SpeakResponse

StockHeatmapRow.description:
One stock's own tile — colored by its close-to-close `pct_change` over `period`, sized by
whichever `size_by` metric `get_stock_heatmap` was asked for. The per-symbol counterpart to
`SectorHeatmapRow`'s per-industry aggregate; `industry` rides along so the frontend can group/
label tiles by sector even though this tool's own ranking is flat across the whole market.
StockHeatmapRow.title: StockHeatmapRow

StockInfoRow.description:
`stock_info` / `stock_info_with_warrant` — one roster row of the Taiwan stock/warrant
universe reference table.
StockInfoRow.title: StockInfoRow

StockNewsRow.description:
`stock_news` — one FinMind-sourced news item for one stock. Third-party content: cite,
never restate as our own analysis. Distinct from the `news` capability's RSS/Finnhub
aggregator (`sources/news.py`) — this is FinMind's own dataset, wired the same as every
other FinMind capability. Free tier; single trading day per request upstream.
StockNewsRow.title: StockNewsRow

StockScoreBreakdown.description:
The 5-factor breakdown for a plain equity. Company-fundamentals-based (value/quality) and
price-technical (momentum/trend) factors — meaningless for an ETF, which has no earnings/
balance sheet of its own (see `EtfScoreBreakdown` for the ETF-specific factor set).
StockScoreBreakdown.title: StockScoreBreakdown

StockSwot.description:
The four SWOT quadrants for the AI-generated stock summary — every bullet is grounded in
one of `ScoreResult.breakdown`'s factors (see `analytics/summary_generation.py`'s prompt),
never fabricated beyond what the score already discloses. Any quadrant may be empty (e.g. no
factor supported a "threats" bullet that day) — an empty tuple, never a filler sentence.
StockSwot.title: StockSwot

StrategySubscription.description:
A user's 策略盯盤 subscription (one per user): which strategies, over every stock today's
screen picks or only one of the user's watchlist groups, and how to be told.
StrategySubscription.title: StrategySubscription

StrategyWatchDataDates.description:
The latest session each input the screen reads has real rows for: the post-close refresh
steps of the daily cycle (股價 17:40, 融資 17:40, 三大法人 20:10). A date behind the list's
session means that refresh has not landed (or the source is failing).
StrategyWatchDataDates.title: StrategyWatchDataDates

StrategyWatchSlot.description:
One intraday check that ran: how many stocks it compared, how many met every trigger, and
how many of those became an alert (met on two checks in a row, guards passed).
StrategyWatchSlot.title: StrategyWatchSlot

SubIndustryHeat.description:
One sub-industry tile — `pct_change` is the simple average close-to-close percentage
change across every one of that sub-industry's member symbols that had a real close on both
days (never a partial figure silently presented as the whole group's), `null` when none did.
`member_count`/`priced_member_count` let a caller show "產業鏈一製藥" or the reference app's
own member-count style label; a large gap between the two means most members had no price
data for this window, which the frontend should treat as a thinner signal.
SubIndustryHeat.title: SubIndustryHeat

SubscriptionRecord.description:
The local `subscriptions` row as a typed value — the record `GET /billing/subscription`
returns and the webhook writes. `tier`/`byok` are derived from the active price_id.
SubscriptionRecord.title: SubscriptionRecord

SupportResistanceLevel.description:
One 支撐/壓力 price level — a swing pivot's price plus which bar index it pivoted at, so
a caller can place the level's h-line/label from `bar_index` alone rather than re-deriving
an offset from `len(bars)`. `kind` is a plain descriptive label ("support"/"resistance"),
never a trading instruction.
SupportResistanceLevel.title: SupportResistanceLevel

SupportResistanceResult.description:
支撐/壓力 levels detected over the supplied bar window — see
`analytics/structure.py::support_resistance_levels` for the swing-pivot detection rule.
Levels are ordered by `bar_index` ascending (oldest pivot first).
SupportResistanceResult.title: SupportResistanceResult

SymbolDirectorySearchRow.description:
`symbol_directory_search` — one ranked match from the ingested `TaiwanStockInfo` roster
(`StockInfoRow`) for a free-text symbol/name query. `instrument_kind` is derived from the
symbol's code shape (`analytics.symbol_universe.classify_symbol_type`), collapsing
leveraged/inverse ETFs into `"etf"` — this is a UI-facing search-result row, not the roster
row itself, so it carries only what a type-ahead result needs.
SymbolDirectorySearchRow.title: SymbolDirectorySearchRow

SymbolQuoteRow.description:
One list row. `change`/`change_pct` are always the DAILY move (latest close vs. the
previous trading day's close), whatever `days` the sparkline spans; `None` when fewer than
two bars exist. `name` is `None` for a symbol absent from the roster, never a placeholder.
SymbolQuoteRow.title: SymbolQuoteRow

SymbolSearchResultRow.description:
`symbol_search` — one `yfinance.Search` quote match for a free-text query (e.g.
"台積電"/"TSMC"→2330.TW; general multi-market name/ticker resolution).
SymbolSearchResultRow.title: SymbolSearchResultRow

SymbolTheme.description:
One row of the reverse lookup — a theme a symbol belongs to, plus that membership's
own sub-industry/confidence for the symbol.
SymbolTheme.title: SymbolTheme

SymbolType.description:
Which scoring branch a symbol belongs to — the discriminator `scoring_batch.py` uses to
pick `StockScoreBreakdown` vs `EtfScoreBreakdown` (see `analytics/models.py`). Plain equities
and ETFs need entirely different factors (an ETF has no ROE/EV-EBITDA of its own; a leveraged/
inverse ETF's daily-rebalancing decay makes the stock-style trend-template actively
misleading, not just unavailable — see the design discussion this module implements).
SymbolType.title: SymbolType

TagScreenerHit.description:
One matched symbol plus the requested tags it actually satisfied — the "show the work"
transparency rule: an `AND` hit lists every requested tag (all satisfied), an `OR` hit lists
the subset it matched. A negated condition that held is reported here in its `not <tag>` form,
so the row is self-explaining without re-deriving the query.
TagScreenerHit.title: TagScreenerHit

TagScreenerResult.description:
The normalized tag-screener response. `detail` is never empty — an empty result still
carries a real, honest reason (no ingested flag partition yet, no symbol matched, an unknown
tag key), never fabricated matches. `total_matches` is the full match count before the `size`
page cap; `hits` is the capped page.
TagScreenerResult.title: TagScreenerResult

ThemeMember.description:
One `theme_memberships` row, as returned by the reverse (symbol -> themes) lookup and
accepted by the snapshot-replace write.
ThemeMember.title: ThemeMember

ThemeSummary.description:
One theme's discovery-card shape — identity plus its member count, so a caller (the
screener's `PresetLibrary`-style theme picker) can show "半導體 (128)" without a second
round-trip per theme.
ThemeSummary.title: ThemeSummary

ThemeTier.description:
One `theme_tiers` row — a sub-industry's upstream/midstream/downstream position within a
theme, plus which producer (curated editorial map or keyword heuristic) assigned it.
ThemeTier.title: ThemeTier

ThinkingBlock.description:
`agent_id` attributes this reasoning chunk to the lane that produced it (`root` for a
non-fanned-out `single`/`none` turn) — needed so a persisted `subagent`/`team` turn's process
trace can be grouped by lane the same way the live SSE view already is.
ThinkingBlock.title: ThinkingBlock

TickSnapshotRow.description:
`tick_snapshot` — one bounded intraday tick-level snapshot. Sponsor-only. `symbol` holds
either a 4-digit stock id or a 3-digit index code (91 documented index codes — broad-market/
sector/themed/leverage — besides ordinary stocks); this is a data_id-taxonomy quirk, not a
stock-only restriction.
TickSnapshotRow.title: TickSnapshotRow

Tier.description:
User subscription tier — gates paid data + throughput only, never a recommendation
(governance.md §9).
Tier.title: Tier

TierSummary.description:
One tier as the pricing page shows it - a projection of the two tables above, so the page
can never promise a limit or feature the enforcement code does not know about.
TierSummary.title: TierSummary

TimingClass.description: How current a SourceResult's data can be. Every result is tagged.
TimingClass.title: TimingClass

TokenBreakdown.description:
Input tokens attributed to each context-composition source for one turn. Every field
defaults to 0 — a source that contributed nothing (e.g. no branch summary was needed) is
recorded as zero, never omitted, so a regression (a summary silently ballooning, a
deferred-tool set stopping being deferred) is visible in the shape itself.
TokenBreakdown.title: TokenBreakdown

ToolCall.description: One normalized tool-call proposal from the model.
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolResultPart.description:
The outcome of a prior tool call, reported back to the model in a `role=tool` message.

`content` is a string (already-rendered tool output) — the LLM adapter does not know or
care about the tool's own typed output model; that normalization happens in `tools/`
(Phase 4), strictly below this layer's concern.
ToolResultPart.title: ToolResultPart

TrailingReturnPoint.description: One horizon of `EtfTrailingReturns`, flattened so a chart can plot the six of them.
TrailingReturnPoint.title: TrailingReturnPoint

Transcript.description:
STT output: text + per-segment confidence. The client shows this for edit; the user
submits the (possibly corrected) text via the normal `POST /agent/query`.
Transcript.title: Transcript

TriggerMode.description:
How often a rule may fire: once then auto-disable, at most once a day, or on every
occurrence (still bounded by cooldown, the daily cap, and the spam auto-pause).
TriggerMode.title: TriggerMode

Turn.description:
One user request -> one agent response cycle. `messages` holds every block on this
turn (already filtered to the active path by the store — a `Turn` itself never carries
an abandoned branch).
Turn.title: Turn

TurnUsage.description: The per-turn accounting snapshot: totals plus the breakdown that explains them.
TurnUsage.title: TurnUsage

TwRankingKind.description:
One tab of the TW-market 排行榜 card (excluding 大戶買賣, wired separately — see module
docstring).
TwRankingKind.title: TwRankingKind

TwRankingRow.description:
One ranked row — the `SymbolQuoteRows`-compatible base (symbol/name/price/change/
change_pct/volume, left `None` here since this tool doesn't itself fetch a live quote; the
frontend enriches via `useSymbolQuotes` the same way `UsMarketRankingRows` does) plus one
shared `extra_value`/`extra_label` pair carrying this kind's own distinct metric — a signed
streak-day count (`dealer_streak`/`trust_streak`/`foreign_streak`), a signed margin-balance
change (`margin_change`), or a plain percentage (`dividend_yield`/`revenue_growth`). One
shared numeric field for all 6 kinds keeps the frontend's row-rendering path uniform.
TwRankingRow.title: TwRankingRow

UpdateAlertRequest.description:
A partial edit. Send only what changed; `null` clears a nullable field (`expires_in_days`,
`cooldown_seconds`, `quiet_hours`, `daily_limit`). `expected_version` is the rule's `version`
as the client last saw it — a mismatch is a 409 so edits from two devices never silently
overwrite each other. The rule's scope (symbol / market / watchlist) cannot be edited, and
unknown fields are rejected (422) rather than silently ignored.
UpdateAlertRequest.title: UpdateAlertRequest

UpdateScheduleRequest.description:
A partial edit. Only sent fields change; `null` clears `quiet_hours`/`daily_limit`.
`expected_version` makes the edit refuse (409 `stale_version`) if another device saved first.
UpdateScheduleRequest.title: UpdateScheduleRequest

UsStockScoreBreakdown.description:
The US-market counterpart to `StockScoreBreakdown` — same `momentum`/`trend_quality`/
`value_guard`/`quality` factors (already market-agnostic, computed straight from price/
financials), but `analyst_revision` in place of `revenue_flow`: US has no 三大法人
institutional-flow/月營收 equivalent ingested anywhere, so rather than let that TW-shaped slot
degrade to permanently unavailable, the fifth factor is a genuinely US-native signal — the
analyst estimate-revision factor (IBES/Zacks-style: EPS-trend delta + revision breadth from
`AnalystConsensus`), a well-documented growth/sentiment factor with no TW equivalent either
(TW's `AnalystConsensus` payload never populates the `_extended` EPS-trend fields this factor

get.description:
Live-ish quote feed (SSE) via the shared demand-driven poller.

One poller per worker fetches each demanded symbol once per tick — through `dispatch_tool`
over `get_price_quote`, exactly the one-shot `/quote` path — and fans the snapshot out to
every subscriber, so N clients watching one symbol cost one upstream fetch, not N. Subscribing
increments a Redis demand refcount; disconnecting decrements it, and at zero the symbol leaves
the demand set so the poller stops touching it (bounded observation, never an unattended
scan). Each `quote` frame carries `as_of` (the snapshot's own source timestamp) and
`market_open`; off-hours the poller idles.

Entitlement is unchanged from the one-shot read: the shared fetch pulls real data, and each
connection re-applies `get_price_quote`'s own masking to its frames (via the same
`MaskedTeaser` shape `dispatch_tool` uses), so an unentitled caller sees the masked teaser per
tick, never a hard error. Over-cap symbols (per-connection or global) are dropped from this
subscription rather than crashing the connection.

get.description:
Attach to a thread's running turn and stream its remaining frames, with durable
`Last-Event-ID` resume when the transport backend supports it.

Two paths, chosen by the configured transport:

- **Same worker (or single-process `memory` backend):** if this worker holds the live turn in
  its registry, attach to the in-process bus directly. Live-only — the in-memory backend has
  no durable/cross-worker log to replay from.
- **Cross worker (`redis` backend):** subscribe to the turn's live Redis channel first, then
  replay everything the client missed from the durable log, then emit live frames — filtering
  out any whose `seq` the replay already covered. A reconnect after the turn ended still
  replays the tail from the durable log.

A reconnect with nothing to attach to and no durable reader returns an immediately-closing
stream rather than an error.

descendant — passing the source user turn's own last message id (the same parent the
original assistant turn was appended under) makes the new assistant turn a sibling of the one
being regenerated, both hanging off the same user message. No new store method was needed;
`append_turn` already supports this shape. The turn-driver invocation is the same
`api.turn_driver.start_turn_stream` seam `/agent/query` uses — same guardrail/entitlement/
journal path, no bypass — seeded with the original turn's user text instead of a fresh
message. `regenerate_of` on the new turn records which turn it re-ran.
